argument_summary: The supportable position on the present admissible record is not clean certification. It is certification with an explicit model-card caveat. The existing evidence supports three points together: aggregate readiness passed, no severity-one rehearsal incidents were recorded, and one named-use-case weakness remains in loan-modification hardship-document checklisting. The draft runbook supports a monitoring posture but does not resolve the weakness or remove disclosure obligations. On that reading, the audited claim should be narrowed to: certification is supportable only if the unresolved limitation is disclosed in release documentation and treated as a monitored post-launch risk, not as a resolved issue.
claims_about_business_cost: Business cost is not the basis for the position and should not control the audit outcome. The argument for certification rests on the admissible readiness evidence plus required disclosure of the unresolved limitation.
claims_about_policy: The supplied policy text cuts against clean certification, but it does not foreclose caveated certification. It says certification without material caveats requires either evidence that no material weakness remains or an approved mitigation with owner, threshold, review date, and rollback criterion. The admissible record does not satisfy that clean-certification standard because the runbook is still draft and the weakness remains unresolved. The policy therefore supports a narrower position: if certification proceeds, it must not state or imply that there are no material limitations, and it must rely on explicit disclosure rather than on the draft runbook as governance cover.
concessions: The current record does not support certification without material caveats.
The draft mitigation artifact is not an approved mitigation under the supplied policy text because owner and alert threshold remain TBD.
The present packet does not prove, by itself, that the final model-card language has already been inserted or approved.
The auditor is reasonable to reject any claim that the issue is resolved or immaterial on the current evidence.
